payload.title: test_merge_index_single_owner recognises a fold of the merged rows only as a comparison with the literal 'merged', so a fold through a named constant (EVENT_MERGED) or a constant set such as auto_merge's _OWNED_LIFECYCLE_EVENTS passes the single-owner pin
evidence: aria-kernel/tests/invariants/test_merge_index_single_owner.py:84-90 (_names_merged accepts a Constant or a literal tuple, list or set, never a Name)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/auto_merge.py:553-559 (a constant frozenset that holds 'merged' already exists in production code)
payload.rule_violated: F3.3a one-owner rule: a second fold of the merged rows must be red the commit it appears (the digest.py pattern); CLAUDE.md tier 3, detectable at build time.
payload.notes: A new module folds merged rows with row['event'] in LIFECYCLE_EVENTS or row['event'] == EVENT_MERGED. _names_merged sees a Name, not a Constant, so merged_row_fold_offenders returns nothing and the invariant stays green while a second merge index exists. The decision comparison at line 139 has the same literal-only blind spot. Close condition: Resolve module-level string constants and constant sets in the scan (a Name bound to a value that holds 'merged'), and add planted shapes for == EVENT_MERGED and in CONSTANT_SET to test_every_shape_the_atlas_named_is_caught that must be red. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
